title: AI-Powered Waste Segregation and Circular Bioeconomy for NSU Green Campus
summary: An intelligent waste classification and circular resource recovery initiative deploying computer-vision smart sorting bins and bioconversion of campus cafeteria organic waste into sustainable bio-fertilizer.
description_html:
Rapid urbanization and institutional campus operations produce complex solid waste streams with low baseline recycling rates. This research develops and field-tests an automated multi-stream segregation infrastructure powered by edge computer-vision models. Smart dustbin prototypes identify, classify, and sort compostable organic materials, recyclable plastics, and municipal refuse at the point of disposal.

Diverted organic fractions from campus cafeterias are subjected to controlled thermophilic composting and anaerobic fermentation, evaluating process kinetics, pathogen inactivation, and nutrient recovery to formulate clean bio-fertilizers supporting sustainable campus landscape ecology.
methodology_html:
1. Computer Vision Sorting: Embedded deep learning classifiers (convolutional neural networks optimized via TensorRT) run on edge microcontrollers paired with high-resolution optical and infrared sensors inside disposal chambers. Automated baffles mechanically route waste into compartmentalized bins.

2. Bioeconomy Assay: Food waste is characterized for volatile solids (VS), chemical oxygen demand (COD), and C:N stoichiometry. Bioreactor trials evaluate decomposition rates, volatile fatty acid generation, and humification indexes under varying aeration regimens.
collaborations: North South University Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, NSU Campus Operations.
